{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
I 'helped' my alcoholic brother for years—covered his rent, made excuses to his employer, cleaned up after his binges. I thought I was being a good sister. His counselor finally told me I'd been making it easy for him to keep drinking. My love was his longest bar tab.

CANDIDATE A:
I proofread every paper for my struggling college student, essentially rewriting them. I thought I was tutoring. After she failed her first exam—something I couldn't take for her—I realized she'd never learned to write because I'd been doing it for her. My help was her handicap.

CANDIDATE B:
I refused to keep covering for my alcoholic brother. When he asked me to call his boss with another excuse, I said no. When he needed rent money after a binge, I offered to pay for rehab instead. He was furious and didn't speak to me for months. But cutting off the enabling forced him to face his addiction. He's been sober for two years now.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:20"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both stories involve a person realizing that their previous attempts to help were actually enabling negative behavior, leading to a decisive change that ultimately benefits the person in need."}
